full_caption: Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere, Appellant, v. Desmond Nettleford, Appellee
court: Westmarch Land and Property Court, Windmere Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere claims title by adverse possession to a 1.4-acre wooded tract adjoining 4858 Sycamore Reach, Windmere, WM, of which Desmond Nettleford is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Tacking is permitted between successive possessors in privity. Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere may tack the 8 years of possession by its predecessor, whose deed purported to convey the disputed tract, to satisfy the statutory term.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Payment of property taxes is not an independent element in this jurisdiction but is evidence bearing on the notoriety of the claim. Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere paid taxes assessed against the tract for 16 of the 21 years in question.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 40.2 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Color of title is not required where the claim rests on actual occupancy, but it enlarges the claim to the full extent of the described premises rather than the portion actually occupied.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere posted the tract against trespass in 1988, cut and sold standing timber in 1999 and 2010, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 50-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Fitzwilliam Jarrowmere's favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Hostility does not require ill will. It requires only that the possession be without the record owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title. A claimant's mistaken belief as to the true line does not defeat hostility in this State.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit B.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — STATEMENT OF CLAIM AND DESCRIPTION
sections.text: Claimant asserts title by adverse possession to a tract of 1.4 acres more particularly described in the surveyor's Exhibit B, being that portion of the record parcel lying east of the posted line and north of the old rail grade, and claims the same in fee simple absolute as against all persons.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ACTS OF POSSESSION RELIED UPON
sections.text: Claimant relies upon the following acts, each continuing from the date shown through the date of filing: posting of the perimeter against trespass beginning in 1988; commercial timber harvest in 1999 and 2010; construction and continuous seasonal use of a hunting camp; annual maintenance of the interior access track; and payment of the real property taxes assessed against the tract for 16 of the 21 years preceding this claim.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.
